newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada regional airline pilots begin strike.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada regional airline pilots begin strike.

text.p: A strike begun Friday by 900 pilots at Air Canada's four regional airlines disrupted scheduled flights at many Canadian airports as carriers scrambled to get passengers to their destinations.

Contract talks between the Canadian Air Line Pilots Association and the regional airlines broke off Thursday, prompting the early morning walkout by pilots at Air Ontario, Air Nova, AirBC and Quebec's Air Alliance.
No new discussions were scheduled, the union and airlines said.
The regional airlines operate mainly between Canada's major cities and smaller population centres.
About 250 pilots set up picket lines at Air Canada's headquarters at Montreal's Dorval airport on Friday, and similar demonstrations were staged at other Canadian airports.
The pilots' union said the main unresolved issue was access by its members to fair and equitable work through the Air Canada system.
The pilots want to be able to retain their seniority if they switch from the regional airlines to Air Canada, Canada's biggest airline.
Air Canada reported no major disruptions to its schedule, but said some flights were being "consolidated."
That meant some scheduled flights on busy routes such as Montreal to Toronto were cancelled to free up planes to assist the regional airlines, Air Canada spokeswoman Kym Robertson said.

Air Ontario, AirBC and Air Nova said they were operating about two-thirds of their schedules and trying to make up the rest by leasing planes from other airlines. Air Ontario's 146 flight attendants walked off the job five days earlier in a separate contract dispute.
Flights from Toronto's city centre airport were suspended, but passengers were to be offered Air Canada flights into Toronto's Lester Pearson International Airport, Air Ontario said.
Air Ontario Service to Baltimore and between Thunder Bay, Ontario and Winnipeg would be suspended during the strike, the airline said. All other routes will receive air service.
Flight delays were also reported at various airports because of heavy snowfall over much of central and eastern Canada.
